policy.admission_complete: Every verifier-domain predicate is DECLARED or DERIVED.
policy.fail_closed: Any NOT_DECLARED verifier-domain predicate yields PROBLEM_UNDERSPECIFIED.
policy.no_repair: The audit records gaps but never adds assumptions to a case dossier.

reclassifications.reason: The contract declares only z != 0.  The exclusion z notin {0,-1,-2,...} cannot be derived from that declaration; knowing the pole set does not declare that the input avoids every pole.
source_basis: NIST DLMF 5.15.5 https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.15.E5
NIST DLMF 5.2.2 https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.2.E2

reclassifications.reason: The entry says only that unspecified regularity assumptions make K_lambda bounded and compact.  It does not state a function space or an explicit condition on V, so the theorem-domain predicate is not declared.
source_basis: Wikipedia Birman-Schwinger principle, statement noting that regularity assumptions on V are required for boundedness and compactness
The dossier's own function_domains.K_lambda entry

rps-r-birman-schwinger-kernel.statement: V satisfies an explicit source-backed function-space hypothesis sufficient for K_lambda to be a bounded compact operator.
rps-r-birman-schwinger-kernel.reason: The dossier uses the placeholder 'regularity so that K_lambda is bounded and compact' and never records the regularity class.  The source itself says such hypotheses are required.
source_basis: Wikipedia Birman-Schwinger principle, statement of the regularity requirement
The dossier's symbol_assumptions.V and function_domains.K_lambda entries

rps-r-fano-beutler-profile.reason: Gamma_res is only described as a line width.  Neither symbol_assumptions nor a predicate declares it nonzero, although the reduced-energy definition divides by it.
source_basis: Miroshnichenko, Flach, and Kivshar, Rev. Mod. Phys. 82 (2010), Eq. (1), arXiv:0902.3014
The dossier's reduced-energy expression

rps-r-fano-beutler-profile.statement: q is real for the asserted real zero, maximum, and one-parameter cross-section profile.
rps-r-fano-beutler-profile.reason: The extrema and zero statements are claims about the real profile, but q has no real-valued declaration.  A physical name is not an assumption under the contract.
source_basis: Miroshnichenko, Flach, and Kivshar, Rev. Mod. Phys. 82 (2010), Eqs. (1)-(2), arXiv:0902.3014
The dossier's symbol_assumptions.q entry

rps-r-lorentz-causal-poles.statement: tau != 0 wherever Gamma = 1/tau or omega/tau is used.
rps-r-lorentz-causal-poles.reason: The contract calls tau a relaxation time but never declares it nonzero or positive.  Physical terminology cannot supply the missing predicate.
source_basis: Wikipedia Lorentz oscillator model, dielectric-function denominator
The dossier's branch convention Gamma_j = 1/tau

rps-r-lorentz-causal-poles.statement: omega0 is a strictly positive real resonance frequency for the claimed strict lower-half-plane pole placement.
rps-r-lorentz-causal-poles.reason: gamma > 0 alone does not imply both roots of omega0**2-omega**2-I*gamma*omega lie strictly in Im(omega)<0 for an unrestricted omega0; omega0=0 already places one root at zero.
source_basis: Capers, Boyes, Hibbins, and Horsley, arXiv:2008.05546, discussion following Eq. (5)
The dossier's pole-placement claim and symbol_assumptions.omega0 entry

rps-r-schrieffer-wolff-denom.statement: For every index k actually included in each displayed second-order sum, each denominator d_i-d_k and d_j-d_k occurring in that summand is nonzero, or the summation exclusions/block restrictions are explicit.
rps-r-schrieffer-wolff-denom.reason: The displayed sums are unqualified sums over k.  Saying that degenerate levels share a block does not specify which k are omitted, and zero matrix elements do not make a written 0/0 quotient defined.
source_basis: Wikipedia Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, component generator and second-order formula
The dossier's two nonzero_conditions and displayed sums

rps-r-schrieffer-wolff-denom.statement: H0 and V are Hermitian (with real d_i) when S is claimed anti-Hermitian and exp(S) is claimed unitary.
rps-r-schrieffer-wolff-denom.reason: The contract uses the physical word Hamiltonian but does not declare Hermiticity or real eigenvalues.  Those properties are required for the anti-Hermitian/unitary claim and may not be supplied as folklore.
source_basis: Wikipedia Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, unitary transformation generated by an anti-Hermitian S
The dossier's symbol_assumptions.H0, symbol_assumptions.V, and function_domains entries

rps-r-weyl-titchmarsh-m.statement: The differential expression, coefficient regularity, self-adjoint realization, and limit-point or boundary condition selecting the Weyl solution are explicit.
rps-r-weyl-titchmarsh-m.reason: The dossier mixes half-line matrix M-functions and a separated-endpoint scalar Green kernel without specifying the underlying operator coefficients or endpoint hypotheses.  A branch-convention sentence naming alternatives does not choose one.
source_basis: Clark and Gesztesy, arXiv:math/9905070, hypotheses preceding Theorem 2.8
The dossier's function_domains.M_plus, function_domains.G, and final branch convention

rps-dp-dexpinv-bernoulli.statement: The spectrum of ad_Omega lies in the Taylor-series convergence disk |w| < 2*pi (or an explicit alternative convergence hypothesis is stated) when dexp_Omega^{-1} is identified with the Bernoulli power series.
rps-dp-dexpinv-bernoulli.reason: Avoiding the poles 2*pi*I*Z\{0} makes dexp invertible, but it does not make the Taylor series about zero converge outside its radius 2*pi.  The contract declares the scalar disk yet does not impose it on ad_Omega.
source_basis: Iserles, Munthe-Kaas, Norsett, and Zanna, Acta Numerica 9 (2000), dexp inverse expansion
Abramowitz and Stegun 23.1.1, Bernoulli generating function
The dossier's analytic_domains entries

rps-dp-liouville-jacobi-cnf.statement: The CNF vector field f has explicit regularity sufficient for a differentiable flow and for Df(x(t),t) and its trace to exist along the trajectory.
rps-dp-liouville-jacobi-cnf.reason: The contract declares regularity of the linear matrix A and positivity of p, but it records no domain or differentiability assumption for the nonlinear CNF vector field f.
source_basis: Chen et al., Neural ODE, arXiv:1806.07366, instantaneous change-of-variables theorem
Grathwohl et al., FFJORD, arXiv:1810.01367, Eq. (2)
The dossier's function_domains and analytic_domains entries

rps-dp-stm-sensitivity-kernel.statement: B(t)u(t) is continuous or otherwise explicitly integrable on the stated interval for the variation-of-parameters member.
rps-dp-stm-sensitivity-kernel.reason: Continuity of A guarantees the state-transition matrix, but it does not guarantee existence of the forcing integral involving B*u.  No regularity for B or u is declared.
source_basis: Rugh, Linear System Theory, variation of parameters
The dossier's variation-of-parameters expression and analytic_domains entries

rps-dp-stm-sensitivity-kernel.statement: x0(theta) is differentiable in theta when S(t0)=d x0/d theta is included.
rps-dp-stm-sensitivity-kernel.reason: C1 regularity of A(t,theta) does not imply differentiability of parameter-dependent initial data.  The displayed initial sensitivity therefore needs its own predicate.
source_basis: Hartman, Ordinary Differential Equations, parameter differentiation
Hairer, Norsett, and Wanner, Solving Ordinary Differential Equations I, Section I.14
The dossier's sensitivity initial condition
